title: Playing lake dates with Papa Dad's quartet
summary: Braud describes his four-piece band with Eddie Gilmore, a clarinetist and guitarist Papa Dad, playing weekend dances at the lake camps and pavilions.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Say, I wanted to ask you about, did you ever know a fella called Dad, Little Dad, they call him?
What did he play, guitar or banjo?
Guitar banjo?
Yeah, yeah, I know him, yeah. Little about that tall, little part of that.
You ever work with him? Sure. Where was that?
Huh?
What was that?
Oh, different places out on the lake and Bucktown, Spanish food, West End. Yeah. And you have a big band? I was a good bass player, too.
Did you have a good band with you or what?
No, we only had four pieces, that's all.
What was it?

Clarinet, guitar and bass. And who were they? A fella by the name of Eddie Gilmore played the bass. And I played the band? And a fella by the name of Al Seed, I don't know his last name, I forgot his last name, but he played the clarinet. And Papa Dad played the guitar.
And who? Papa Dad?
We used to call him Papa Dad. We used to call him Papa Dad.
Well who's?
He lived up in the garden. The fella by that high. Well the whole family was musical. He had a brother who used to get on the box and play the bass. And he had a brother who was a clarinet player.
But who's T-Boy? T-Boy played bass.

And who is he? He died in Eddie Gilmore. That's Eddie Gilmore. He's a good bass player. I left them playing together when I left him. That's the guy who played the bass, T-Boy. And you were playing mandolin? Yeah.
Well did y'all stay in one place or did you serenade?

Oh no, we just played dates on Saturdays and Sunday out in the season. Right on the lake. He used to have them little camps bill out there. I don't know if they're still there. Little dancing pavilion. Some out the long way.
He had a board walk.
He'd walk out there in the lake. And he used to give picnics out there. Well did you have a play with these groups that walk around from places?
No, no I didn't go for that.
You met them yet?
Yeah, I didn't go for that. Too much walking?
Well, no. Sometimes you run up in bad spots and you're kind of like, you know, you're not saying that kind of thing.
Oh, you wanted to hear Snagget, didn't you?
